nodes.label: @heliogrid/web — Next.js App Router, pure frontend/BFF
nodes.rationale: Route handlers exist ONLY for cookie/session BFF glue; everything domain-shaped calls apps/api through the ts-rest client, and shared decisions are imported from @heliogrid/domain rather than authored here.

nodes.label: app/ ROUTES, features/ OWNS
nodes.rationale: A page.tsx body is ≤50 lines (Biome noExcessiveLinesPerFunction): read route params, call one controller hook, render one screen. A feature is named for the CAPABILITY it owns, matching the API module that serves it so one name spans both sides.

nodes.label: Features imported only through a barrel
nodes.rationale: features/<feature>/index.ts or a screen barrel one level down — nothing deeper, enforced by dependency-cruiser.

nodes.label: A barrel must not mix a Server Component and a 'use client' screen
nodes.rationale: Next attaches the client screen's chunk to EVERY page reaching the barrel and tree-shaking cannot remove it — /design shipped the whole gallery at 147 kB against a 102 kB baseline (2026-07-31). Symptom: two routes reporting IDENTICAL First Load JS.

nodes.label: "sideEffects": ["**/*.css"] is load-bearing
nodes.rationale: Each screen imports its own CSS, which is a side effect, so without the declaration webpack keeps every module a barrel names — all three auth routes shipped an identical 183 kB (2026-07-31).

nodes.label: lib/api-client.ts is the ONLY path — never hand-roll fetch
nodes.rationale: An untyped api<T>() with a hand-declared response type made contract drift invisible to typecheck; api-client rejects on non-2xx so a resolved value is always the declared success body. Read error copy with envelopeMessage(err).

nodes.label: Enum-driven pickers iterate schema.options
nodes.rationale: Onboarding's SEGMENTS was an as-const array — merely subset-assignable — so a new tenantSegmentSchema value compiled green while being unselectable in the UI.

nodes.label: lib/env.ts must write process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_* out LITERALLY
nodes.rationale: Next substitutes textually at build time, so process.env[key] or a spread reads undefined in the browser and silently falls back to the schema default — a production URL would be ignored with nothing failing.

nodes.label: /design renders dist/tokens.json
nodes.rationale: A token that doesn't render there doesn't exist.
